# Tyre pressure

## The numbers

From the placard on the driver's door pillar of the Astra (205/55 R16):
- Normal load: 32 psi front, 30 psi rear (2.2 / 2.1 bar)
- Full load (4 people + luggage): 35 psi front, 41 psi rear
- Spare is a space saver: 60 psi, max 50 mph

Winter set on the steel wheels: same pressures, but they leak down about 2 psi a month because of the old valves. Put new valves in next time. Winter set details in [[Winter tyres]].

## Kit

- Ring RAC610 cordless inflator, £44.99, auto stops at the set pressure. Lives in the shed
- Michelin stick gauge in the glovebox as a cross check. The inflator reads 1 psi high
- Check cold, before driving, first Sunday of the month

## TPMS light

The Astra doesn't have pressure sensors, it uses the ABS wheel speed sensors to spot a tyre turning faster (smaller rolling radius). So after inflating you have to reinitialise it: ignition on, hold the TPMS button on the dash until it chimes. Forgot that twice and the light came back on.

## Slow puncture, March 2025

- Rear nearside down to 22 psi after a week
- Soapy water spray found a screw in the centre of the tread
- Kwik Fit Fishponds repaired it to BS AU 159, £22, job ref KF-FP-30017. Fine because it was in the central 3/4 of the tread
- Sidewall damage can't be repaired, would've been a new tyre

## Tread

Legal minimum 1.6mm across the central 3/4. I replace at 3mm. Pressures and tread go on the list before any long trip, see [[Road trip car checklist]].
